title: Chainguard Hits 1 Billion Container Builds With AI-Powered Software Supply Chain
content_md: Chainguard has surpassed one billion container build manifests, doubling its output from 500 million in six months as it scales its AI-assisted, self-correcting software supply chain platform . The milestone also covers more than 3,000 unique container images and 675,000 image versions, reflecting the challenge of keeping cloud-native artifacts current amid constant upstream code, dependency, architecture, and security changes. A build manifest represents every new verifiable artifact produced by the Chainguard Factory. This includes a newly released language image, a rebuild triggered by a libc patch, an architecture-specific variant, or a regenerated software bill of materials (SBOM) after a dependency update. Chainguard Hits 1 Billion Container For heavily used projects such as Python, dozens of supported versions across multiple architectures can require repeated rebuilding as upstream packages evolve. rebuild velocity (Source: chainguard) The company said this continuous rebuild model is designed to address a key gap in conventional vulnerability management . Rather than securing an image only when it is initially pulled, Chainguard aims to ensure that images remain rebuilt, signed, and updated throughout their lifecycle. Chainguard’s build pipeline starts with Chainguard OS, its Linux distribution designed for cloud-native workloads and rolling software delivery.
